newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe hospitals stay shut as strike continues.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe hospitals stay shut as strike continues.

text.p: Zimbabwe's two major government hospitals were shut for the second day running on Thursday due to a crippling strike by nurses and junior doctors.

"On the whole, nothing is happening here. You have some activity in one or two wards, but for all practical purposes the hospital is closed," said an official at the country's largest medical centre, Harare Hospital.

Harare and Parirenyatwa Hospitals, also in the capital, closed their doors to patients on Wednesday after junior doctors, operating theatre staff and physiotherapists went on strike to protest at the arrest of two of their colleagues over a two-week strike by nurses.
Doctors Farai Jiah and Austin Bene -- both leaders of the state Hospitals Doctors Association facing charges on inciting the strike -- were later freed on Wednesday.
A Harare magistrate said he needed time to decide whether to refer their case to the Supreme Court as their lawyer had raised constitutional issues during an initial remand hearing.

Union officials, who say there are 10,000 nurses on strike for higher pay countrywide, were unavailable for comment on Thursday, but acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said would meet the officials later in the day to discuss the strike.

President Robert Mugabe's government is under pressure to resolve the strike which has paralysed many public health facilities across the southern African state, and placed heavy pressure on its small private health system.
The government says it is ready to look at the strikers' demands for higher pay and working conditions if they go back to work.
It reacted to the nurses' strike by firing them last week and is currently advertising for replacements.
